1) How does Redwood amortize a 3-year upfront payment across the term (accounting for usage vs committed capacity)?
2) If FinPath terminates after year 1, what (if any) refund or credit is available? Are there standard "sunset credits" or an escrow mechanism?

Subject: Re: Questions on multi-year commit amortization and exit credits

Hi Samantha — appreciate the usage file, that helps. High level answers and a couple of options for procurement to consider below. Happy to jump on a short call if that speeds things up.

Option A — Standard amortization + capped refund (recommended for customers wanting price stability):
- Upfront prepay is amortized on a straight-line basis over the full contract term for accounting and unit-price purposes.
- Early termination refund = remaining unamortized prepay minus an administrative & risk buffer (standard buffer = 15% of remaining unamortized amount).
- Refund settlement timeline: net 45 days; Redwood retains right to deduct outstanding usage over last billing period.

Option B — Escrowed sunset credits (recommended for larger accounts requesting stronger downside protections):
- Portion of prepay (typ. 20–40%) placed in a 3rd-party escrow, released to customer on a declining schedule if usage drops below thresholds.
- Escrow release tied to a simple threshold: if average utilization >= 70% of committed capacity over a rolling 90-day window, no escrow payout; if < 70%, fraction of escrow released proportional to shortfall.
- This preserves revenue predictability for both parties and avoids large cash refunds.

Co-terming / Renewal consideration:
- If FinPath holds other Redwood contracts that would benefit from aligning renewal dates, we can apply a co-term credit that accelerates amortization of a portion of the prepay to match the shorter term.

Example calculation (3-year, $900k prepay, termination after 14 months):
- Straight-line amortization per month = $900k / 36 = $25k
- Amortized over 14 months = $350k consumed; remaining unamortized = $550k
- Option A refund = $550k - 15% buffer ($82.5k) = $467.5k (subject to final reconciliation and usage).

I'll put together a short term sheet (v2) with both options and a redline snippet procurement/legal can reuse. 

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni

Thanks Vivek — that framing is helpful. Procurement has two follow-ups:

- Can Redwood cap the total cash refund on early termination to a percentage (e.g., no more than 40% of remaining unamortized) rather than applying an open buffer percentage? Procurement wants a predictable maximum exposure.
- If we choose escrow, procurement asks about escrow admin fees and whether Redwood can be the escrow agent (they prefer a neutral 3rd party).

Also, legal is likely to ask for a concrete contract clause they can redline — we can share that with you. Would it be possible to include an example that ties refunds to usage shortfall rather than time only? For example: refund = (remaining unamortized) * (1 - min(1, average_utilization/committed_utilization)).

We can make time for a 30-min sync next week if that helps.

— Samantha

Hi Samantha — looping in sales ops to propose language and a workable settlement process. Attached is a proposed term sheet (v2) with two alternatives and an attached redline excerpt for the contract. Key operational points: 

- Escrow admin: we suggest a neutral escrow (e.g., PrimeTrust). Fee can be split 50/50 for deals over $500k; for smaller deals Redwood absorbs the first $2k of admin fees.
- Cap approach: we can agree to a maximum cash refund of 40% of remaining unamortized prepay (if Option A chosen). That cap replaces the fixed buffer.
- Usage-linked refund formula: we can support the formula Samantha suggested; legal will want a defined measurement window (we recommend 90-day rolling average) and a reconciliation clause that allows final invoice adjustments.
- Co-term credit example included: if FinPath co-terms a 12-mo contract to align with an existing 24-mo contract, Redwood will apply an accelerated amortization of up to 25% of the remaining prepay to the shorter term (one-time credit applied to renewal).

Attached: proposed_term_sheet_v2.pdf, redline_contract_excerpt.docx

Subject: RE: Questions on multi-year commit amortization and exit credits — proposed next steps

Samantha / Kyle — summary and proposed path forward so procurement/legal have a single-working-offer: 

1) Commercial: 3-year $900k prepay; amortized monthly (straight-line).
2) Refund mechanism: capped cash refund at 35% of remaining unamortized prepay if customer terminates early (replaces flat buffer).
3) Usage-linked adjustment: final refund is multiplied by (1 - min(1, avg_90d_util / committed_util)) to reflect actual usage gap.
4) Escrow option: customer may elect 25% of prepay into neutral escrow (PrimeTrust). Fees split 50/50 for deals > $500k; Redwood covers first $2k for smaller deals.
5) Co-terming: if customer requests co-term, Redwood will provide an accelerated amortization credit up to 25% of remaining prepay to realign renewal dates.
6) Notice & settlement: 60 days' termination notice; refund payment within 45 days after reconciliation.

Proposed contract redline snippet (suggested legal language you can drop into the SOW):
"If Customer terminates this Agreement for convenience, Customer shall be eligible for a cash refund equal to the lesser of (a) thirty-five percent (35%) of the remaining unamortized Prepaid Amount, or (b) the Remaining Unamortized Prepaid Amount multiplied by (1 - Avg90DayUtilization/CommittedUtilization). Refunds will be subject to reconciliation for actual usage and shall be paid within forty-five (45) days of the effective date of termination, following settlement of any outstanding invoices"

Next steps: Laura will publish a DocuSign package with the term sheet + redline excerpt and the proposed SOW language. Rafael will run the final numbers against FinPath's Q3 ramp and confirm whether the escrow option materially changes expected unit economics. If that looks OK we request a PO and will provision a test account for immediate onboarding.

Let me know if that matches what procurement needs; happy to join legal call if they want to discuss the exact clause wording.
